A1.evidence: Paper states code is fully deposited and openly available ('All code and data are available here', p.3); Zenodo access_right='open' for the deposit.

A1_1.evidence: Open HTTPS DOI resolution, no login/subscription/proprietary software required to retrieve the code.

A1_2.evidence: Fully open resource requiring no authentication satisfies A1.2 per v2.1 open-case rule; no access control present or warranted.

A2.evidence: Row 2 Zenodo persistence entitlement applies identically to the code portion of the combined deposit.

F1.evidence: Code is deposited in the same combined Zenodo record as the data ('All code and data are available here: https://zenodo.org/records/10623550', p.3), carrying the same own-artefact DOI confirmed by the DataCite record (identifier_in_metadata=true).

F2.evidence: Same Zenodo/DataCite structured metadata (publisher, publication_year, resource_type) covers the combined code+data deposit (Row 2 platform entitlement).

F3.evidence: 'identifier_in_metadata': true for the combined deposit housing the code.

F4.evidence: Same Zenodo/DataCite indexing applies to the code within the combined deposit ('state': 'findable').

I1.evidence: Code is written in R, an open-source, standard, portable scripting language: 'All analyses were performed in the open-source R programming environment (v.4.2.2; R Core Team, 2021), using the Quanteda package (Benoit et al., 2018)' (p.3) — non-proprietary, formal, shared representation for source code.

I2.evidence: No controlled software vocabulary, ontology, or standardised dependency-naming scheme evidenced for the code artefact.

I3.evidence: No qualified typed references (e.g. dependency PIDs, DataCite relatedIdentifiers) evidenced linking the code deposit to other resources; the Quanteda dependency is cited only as a plain bibliographic reference in the article's reference list, not as a machine-qualified reference in the deposit's own metadata.

R1.evidence: The paper documents the code's operation in detail: skip-distance parameter (k=13), PMI formula, package and R version used (Section 2.2, p.3) — functioning as substantive documentation of the deposited scripts.

R1_1.evidence: The same CC-BY-4.0 licence recorded on the combined Zenodo deposit applies to the code files (licences: ['cc-by-4.0']); a clear, identified licence, albeit a content licence rather than an OSI software licence.

R1_2.evidence: Software version and dependency documented: 'the open-source R programming environment (v.4.2.2; R Core Team, 2021), using the Quanteda package (Benoit et al., 2018)' (p.3).

R1_3.evidence: No CITATION.cff, CodeMeta, formal package structure, or community review (CRAN, JOSS, rOpenSci) evidenced for the authors' own code — it is a set of analysis scripts in a generic Zenodo deposit, not a reviewed or packaged software artefact. (The Quanteda dependency is itself JOSS-published, but that credential attaches to a third-party tool, not to the authors' own code.)

A1.evidence: Zenodo API records show 'access_right': 'open' for both version DOIs; paper text confirms open availability ('All code and data are available here', p.3; Data Availability Statement, p.8). Data-completeness coverage computed as 'complete' (100%), so the completeness override does not zero A1.

A1_1.evidence: Open HTTPS DOI resolution via Zenodo; access_right 'open' with no login, subscription, or proprietary software required.

A1_2.evidence: Fully open resource requiring no authentication satisfies A1.2 per v2.1 ('the protocol supports authentication where needed, and none is needed'); no access-control mechanism is present or warranted.

A2.evidence: Row 2 Zenodo platform entitlement (rung ii): tombstone page and metadata persistence guaranteed for the lifetime of the repository even upon withdrawal, corroborated by the 'findable'-state DataCite records for both version DOIs.

F1.evidence: In-text: 'All code and data are available here: https://zenodo.org/records/10623550' (p.3); Data Availability Statement links https://zenodo.org/records/10801706 (p.8). Both DOIs resolve to DataCite records with identifier_in_metadata=true — the deposit carries its own persistent DOI, not merely the article DOI (own-PID deposit, 4/4 F tier).

F2.evidence: Zenodo/DataCite records for both version DOIs show metadata_record=true with publisher ('Zenodo'), publication_year (2024), and resource_type ('Dataset') populated — structured metadata beyond a bare filename, corroborated by the Row 2 Zenodo platform entitlement (DataCite metadata guaranteed by construction).

F3.evidence: 'identifier_in_metadata': true recorded for both the DataCite and Zenodo API records of 10.5281/zenodo.10623550 and 10.5281/zenodo.10801706.

F4.evidence: Deposit hosted on Zenodo (DataCite-indexed, searchable registry); both DataCite records carry 'state': 'findable'.

I1.evidence: Paper states 'Dedicated R code and complete data tables are reported in Supplementary Information S2 and S3' (p.3) — tabular data used directly as input to the R/quanteda skipgram-PMI computational pipeline, indicating structured (non-PDF-image) tabular format rather than unstructured prose or scanned images.

I2.evidence: No FAIR-compliant controlled vocabulary (e.g. ARIADNEplus, Getty AAT, Darwin Core) evidenced. Motif codes (A1, A2, B10, etc.) follow 'Płonka's (2003, pp. 315-325) own motif classification scheme' (p.2) — an idiosyncratic, non-PID-bearing typology, not a published FAIR vocabulary.

I3.evidence: No qualified, typed references (e.g. DataCite relatedIdentifiers linking the deposit to the article DOI or to Płonka 2003) are evidenced in either the paper text or the evidence-pack DataCite/Zenodo records — no related-identifier fields are present in the harvested metadata.

R1.evidence: Section 2.1 'Data preparation' documents the dataset's attributes at length: 'numerous categorical variables corresponding to the characteristics of each ornamented object and associated metadata such as location, quality of contextual information, and original source' (p.2) — a plurality of documented attributes accompanying the artefact.

R1_1.evidence: Zenodo/DataCite records list licences: ['cc-by-4.0'] for both 10.5281/zenodo.10623550 and 10.5281/zenodo.10801706 (access_right: open); consistent with the article's own CC BY 4.0 licence.

R1_2.evidence: Detailed extraction/transformation provenance given in Section 2.1: manual digitisation from Płonka (2003), transcription to binary presence/absence coding by motif type, and transformation into a 'sentence-imitating structure' for skipgram analysis (p.2).

R1_3.evidence: Row 2 platform entitlement: Zenodo deposits generate DataCite metadata by construction, qualifying under R1.3 route (a) 'generic metadata schemas (DataCite, Dublin Core)'.

Both DOIs (10.5281/zenodo.10623550, 10.5281/zenodo.10801706) share the same Zenodo concept DOI (10.5281/zenodo.10623549) per the evidence pack, i.e. they are version-DOIs of the same combined data+code deposit.
